endorsements.quote: While employing the HITL and AITL frameworks, it is important to define not only the role and capabilities of AI but also to explicitly determine the role, expertise level, and responsibilities of the human collaborators.
These limitations highlight the importance of complementing LLMs with reliable external data using tools like RAG [ 25 ] or Graph RAG [ 82 , 83 ].

unlisted_practices: Tailor Gen-AI tools to established HEOR tasks rather than altering the domain to fit the technology.
Restrict AI decision-making and keep decisions largely with human experts to reduce unintentional data biases.
Develop explainable AI models tailored to HEOR so stakeholders, including regulators and payers, can understand and trust AI-generated insights.
Conduct proof-of-concept and real-world validation studies of human-in-the-loop and AI-in-the-loop approaches in specific HEOR workflows.
Encourage collaboration between HEOR professionals, data scientists, and AI developers to optimize AI systems for healthcare needs.
Weigh the added time and cost of Graph RAG against standard RAG before implementation.
Determine the level of human expertise required for each task deliberately at the outset, aligned with task complexity and criticality.

screen.reason: The paper introduces a conceptual hybrid intelligence framework and recommendations for integrating Generative AI into health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) workflows rather than reporting an empirical evaluation.
